_comment: Runs after blip-rear-paint.json. Blip's lid is a flat rectangular panel with two rows of bolts along its long edges, and the panel is SOLID — no holes, no cutouts. The scan got the panel right and the bolts wrong: each bolt pulled the silhouette outward, so the two long edges came out as a comb of teeth with the bolt heads smeared into the notches between them. Highlighting the part on its own shows it plainly, a red rectangle with a serrated fringe down both sides. Crop back to the panel's real edge and the teeth go with it; the bolts stay, because they sit inboard on the face and were never the thing sticking out. The lid hinges about X, so its long edges are at constant x and an axis-aligned cut is the right cut — no oblique plane needed. x is taken from the cross-sections: the flat panel runs -0.114 to 0.106 at every z I sampled, and everything past that is 0.05 deep skirt on the left and 0.03 of ripple on the right. The short edges are left alone: the rear one wanders 0.016 but it is also where the catalog's MEASURED hinge sits, and trimming it stood the panel half an inch off its own pivot. It tucks under the shell in any case.

Part 10 is a ragged strip lying along the lid's right bolt row — scan spill off the seam rather than a component. Nothing of it reads except that strip: the rest is buried inside the shell, and with it gone the bolts on that side render as discrete heads instead of a broken black line. The reference has no raised rail there, only the bolts and the gasket seam the texture already carries.

The hinge is the white axle across the top of the bot, which is part 16. The partitioner's pivotOverride had been sitting at [0,-0.02,-0.266] — the lid's own rear edge, and 0.18 BELOW it. Rotating a panel about a point two thirds of a foot under itself does not hinge it, it swings it up and back off the body, which is why firing the flipper opened a hole into Blip's interior. A y-z cross-section of part 16 at |x|<0.03 draws a clean round shell 0.07 across centred on y 0.158, z -0.292; that circle is the shaft.

And the axle travels with the panel it carries, so part 16 joins modelWeapon. A cylinder turning about its own axis shows nothing, but leaving it behind on the body would part it from the lid the moment the lid moved.
